subject: Adding time dimension to matern2d model

messages.author: 6488b93c40082e2c
messages.subject: Adding time dimension to matern2d model
parts:
Hi All,

I am currently fitting a matern2d model over a square space of 101x101. The coordinates are indexed from 1 to 10201 and the observations are something like number of occurences at each coordinate. From this model I am getting proper 2d maps of a season long trend.

The data also has a time component and I would like to derive a time series of maps over the season. Say I have observations from 10 days, I would like to find 10 separate maps for the days. At the moment I can fit the data points for each day separately and get different maps but that means the correlation between them is 0, i.e. there is no temporal trend.

How can I include/add a time component in the matern2d model? Can I use the outputs of the matern2d model for a rw1 model?

Hope I have framed the question right. Any help would be highly appreciated.

Regards,
Anindya

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Adding time dimension to matern2d model
parts:
There is a feature known as "group" where you can group a space model with a time model. 

This paper has information on that I believe.
Estimation and extrapolation of time trends in registry data—borrowing strength from related populations
A Riebler, L Held, H Rue

Does anyone know further resources on the "group" feature?

Haakon

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Adding time dimension to matern2d model
parts:
See for example the Cameletti et al paper and case study:
http://r-inla.org/examples/case-studies/cameletti-et-al

It uses inla.spde2.matern instead of matern2d, but the group part for space-time modelling is the same. It's not an ideal example for you, since you already have matern2d code, but hopefully the group part of the paper should be clear enough to adapt.

Finn
